speaker: Doctor
text: I'm Dr. Agent. To begin your evaluation for acute diarrhea, have you had any recent travel to foreign countries or eaten undercooked foods?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details, as the recent levofloxacin use strongly suggests antibiotic-associated diarrhea. Are you experiencing any fever, blood in your stool, or signs of severe dehydration? Also, have you noticed any specific triggers or patterns in the timing of your bowel movements?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) secondary to levofloxacin therapy.

REQUEST TEST: C. diff toxin assay (stool).
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_CXR (to assess for complications like toxic megacolon if clinical suspicion remains high, though stool testing is primary).
